The score state (MATCH-22 r22, T400): regulation is read as `segments` consecutive time segments (at most six). A side's open-play chances in a segment are kept by the lead it starts the segment with (own goals minus the opponent's, clamped to ±`cap`): at the base rate × `e^(−volume × lead)`, so a side behind shoots more and a side ahead less, and a goal of a side ahead `e^(risk × lead)` times as often again, the space a chasing side leaves. Chances are drawn `e^(max(|volume|, |risk − volume|) × cap)` times as often first (an arrival's chance still at most 0.9), and each is kept at its share over the factor it was drawn at, so a level score keeps the base rate and no share exceeds one. One ordered pass on its own stream, after every chance is drawn and before the set pieces; set-piece goals do not move the state. One segment is the joint draw without a score state. T400 keeps six segments, volume 0.4 and risk 0.4: against the grid on the same fixtures the team-match correlations shots~goals 0.480 → 0.242 (grid 0.239), xG~goals and key passes~assists become equivalent, draws too, with goals and shots held.
